evals.name: rpath-ctest-failure
evals.prompt: My SYCL tests compile fine but when I run them under ctest they all fail with: error while loading shared libraries: libsycl.so.9: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory. Running the binary by hand in my terminal works. What's going on and how do I fix it properly so CI works too?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses that the toolchain libs aren't on the default loader path and ctest doesn't inherit the activated shell; fixes with a baked-in -Wl,-rpath (not just LD_LIBRARY_PATH), ideally via target_link_options. Bonus: notes the route difference.

evals.name: esimd-cpu-reality
evals.prompt: Write me a small Intel ESIMD example (just a vector add is fine), compile it with icpx and run it here so I can confirm my setup works.
evals.expected_output: Compiles successfully, attempts to run, and correctly reports that ESIMD cannot run on this CPU-only box because it requires the ext_intel_esimd aspect (Intel GPU only) - rather than thrashing on the error or claiming success. Should verify with sycl-ls / an aspect query.

evals.name: route-choice-writeup
evals.prompt: A colleague is spinning up a fresh container for this project and needs icpx working. Write them a short setup note: exactly what to run, and if there's more than one way to install it, which one they should pick and why. Our tests run under ctest in CI.
evals.expected_output: Presents both routes (Intel apt repo and conda-forge), and recommends conda-forge BECAUSE ctest/CI runs binaries without a sourced environment and only the conda route produces relocatable binaries via -rpath. Mentions verifying with sycl-ls.
